text: My colleague, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, will share more details later.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For children of schooling age, we want to give every child access to learning opportunities, regardless of their abilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In her COS speech on Monday, Second Minister for Education Indranee Rajah already elaborated about support for these students in mainstream schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We know that transportation is a key enabler and have put in place various schemes and subsidies to support persons with special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: These include the VWO Transport Subsidy and the Taxi Subsidy Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Government is also continually improving the accessibility and inclusivity of public transportation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: One such example is the School-to-Work Transition Programme, which matches students who are able to work, to suitable training and employment pathways based on their strengths and interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For jobseekers with special needs, MSF and SG Enable will continue to work with MOE and MOM to enhance their employability, expand employment options, and also to promote inclusive hiring.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue to help persons with special needs prepare themselves for the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For example, SG Enable works closely with the Society for the Physically Disabled (SPD), Autism Resource Centre (ARC) and the Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore (MINDS) to match individuals to suitable jobs and help them adjust well into the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I am, therefore, heartened that efforts by the Government, community and corporate partners are bearing fruit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: However, there is still a lot more that we can do together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I, therefore, thank Ms Denise Phua for her suggestions to identify, individualise, integrate, implement and also inspect the caregiver support system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We know that a caregiver’s job is never an easy one.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Indeed, support for caregivers is another key focus of EMP3.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is why we launched the Caregivers Pod at the Enabling Village last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is a place for caregivers to find peer support, and also to attend training sessions and organise sharing sessions among themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To respond to this need, SG Enable is developing a new online portal that will enable caregivers to find relevant resources easily, including for respite care, as suggested by Dr Tan Wu Meng.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MSF agrees that formal respite services are needed to provide temporary relief for caregivers to prevent burnout.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The Drop-in Disability Programme is a day respite option for caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MSF-funded Disability Homes also offer residential respite care services to those who need it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Although these measures will provide welcome support, we also know that many caregivers worry about what will happen to their loved ones when they are older.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I will speak more about this later in my speech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: For now, I will speak on MSF's forward plans to enable persons with special needs to maximise their potential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: She also suggested that the Enabling Masterplans have to be "living documents", and more people and organisations should be co-opted to co-shape and co-implement solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Doing so will not only allow us to better coordinate and provide targeted support to meet the varied needs of differently-abled persons across disability groups but also increase awareness of the Enabling Masterplans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We must prepare our citizens with special needs for the jobs of today and also tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I am, therefore, very grateful that Ms Denise Phua has very kindly agreed to co-chair this workgroup with me to study this issue further with the relevant stakeholders in the public, private and people sectors, including WSG and e2i.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, all of us want to have assurance that the needs of our loved ones, and those of our own, will continue to be met when we enter our senior years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This includes planning for their future expenses for accommodation, health and other care needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Darryl David has asked about support measures for those who have lost their mental capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: All Singaporeans need to plan for our own golden years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Having a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) will give us peace of mind, knowing that a trusted loved one is empowered to act for us should we lose mental capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It will also enable our caregivers to act confidently in providing care for us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will consider this in our ongoing review of the LPA form.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Yet, there are a number of seniors who may not have the support of family members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: They may be single or married but childless.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: MSF has introduced two community support options to help these Singaporeans plan ahead in the event of them losing their mental capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To assure individuals that their interests will be protected, we have put in place a training course for PDDs, and also put in place very robust measures to ensure all the regulations and practices are monitored.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, may I display a slide on the screen?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The scheme allows partner-VWOs to manage the day-to-day expenses of a senior who has lost mental capacity, through the authority of a Court order, and also under the close supervision of the Office of Public Guardian.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This could include passing the senior a fixed cash amount from his bank account so that he can buy food and groceries and make payment for the senior’s utility bills so that he will not experience a disruption in electricity and water supply.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: With the help from a community kin, the senior can stay within the community that he is familiar with, while receiving dedicated care.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, with these schemes in place, we hope that Singaporeans will be able to prepare for their future and also be supported through their golden years.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to now speak in Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: (In Mandarin):   Our vision is to develop an inclusive society where every Singaporean is empowered to participate fully as integral and contributing members.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We have been working towards this objective in the past few years, striving to build a society with bigger hearts, where every individual has hope for a good future, regardless of age and ability.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Members in this House may remember that we laid the groundwork for an inclusive society when we first launched the Enabling Masterplan in 2007.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: In 2012, we enhanced services and support for persons with special needs under the second Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We know that caregiving is both physically and psychologically exhausting.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Therefore, one of the priorities of EMP3 is to help caregivers provide better care for themselves and their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The first workgroup will focus on improving the quality of life for persons with special needs through technology and design.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I will be co-chairing this group with the President of SPD and former NMP Ms Chia Yong Yong.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: I will also co-chair another workgroup with Parliamentary colleague and President of ARC, Ms Denise Phua.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: The aim of this workgroup is to prepare persons with special needs for the future economy by enhancing access to lifelong learning opportunities and employment pathways.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Every one of us would like to live well in our golden years, and every Singaporean should prepare ahead for this stage in life.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: It is for this purpose that we established the LPA.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: By appointing an LPA, we authorise a family member or trusted friend to make decisions on our behalf in the event that we lose our mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: With this clarity, we and our caregivers would have less to worry about.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: At the same time, we are also aware that there are senior citizens with no one to turn to and may not have any caregivers to take care of them should they lose their mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: They may be married but childless or they may be single.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Therefore, MSF has introduced two community support schemes to help these Singaporeans plan ahead.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Under this scheme, individuals can procure the services of a registered PDD to make decisions on their behalf, for example, liquidating their property to finance their care.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: To assure individuals that their interests will be protected, we have put in place robust safeguards.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: These include mandating PDDs to report regularly to the Office of Public Guardian, and record all decisions made on behalf of their clients.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We also provide training for the PDDs to ensure that they are trustworthy and able to support their clients.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This scheme allows partner-VWOs to manage the day-to-day expenses of a senior who has lost mental capacity through the authorisation of a Court order.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This could include VWOs making monthly withdrawals from the senior’s bank account, passing the senior a fixed cash amount so that he can buy food and groceries, or paying for his medical bills.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Doctors have certified that he no longer has the mental capacity to manage his daily expenses.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Under the CKS pilot, a social worker from the authorised VWO helps him pay his utility bills and visits him twice a week to give him an allowance, so that he can continue with his current lifestyle, for example, eating his favourite meals at nearby coffee shops.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: With help from a community kin, this senior can age within the community that he is familiar with while receiving dedicated care.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: This scheme is run by the Office of Public Guardian to ensure that seniors’ monies will not be misused.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: With these schemes, we hope that Singaporeans will prepare ahead for their future and be supported through their golden years.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, all of us can play a part in fostering a caring and inclusive society for all Singaporeans, regardless of their age and ability.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, this is one journey where I hope Singaporeans, particularly those who are interested in and have concerns for persons with disabilities or different abilities, can partner us to walk this journey together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, I thank Members for their valuable suggestions and support for MSF's work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Allow me to start with a few words in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   We, in MSF, are committed to work together to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of the main priority areas is ensuring that every child has a good start in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Preschool education helps children develop skills in thinking, learning and socialising with other children, as well as self-confidence and independence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to ensure affordable and quality early childhood services that are easily accessible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our goal is to ensure that every child has a good start to succeed in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Among the efforts implemented include funding for some preschool operators to offer quality programmes at an affordable fee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also maintain the amount of subsidy received for a longer period, without requiring a review every year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope these enhancements will give families more certainty and peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With more support available for our families, I urge more parents to enrol their children in preschools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ensure your child has a good start in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As we continue to enhance preschool services, some of our children may need more help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To help young children with developmental needs, early intervention is critical to help them achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Currently, the Government provides subsidies for early intervention programmes to help children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: More families will also be paying as little as only $5.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From July onwards, we will also enhance the early intervention programmes so that they are more customised to our children's needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, I have shared our efforts to give all children a good start in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Please allow me to recite a Malay pantun.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Board the LRT at Fajar station To Mandai Zoo we go The young get an education To be smart adults, they grow Ladies and gentlemen, let us journey together to build a better tomorrow for us and our generations ahead.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, quality early childhood development builds strong foundations for life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: My Ministry strives to give every child a good start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since National Day Rally 2012, we have significantly enhanced access to affordable and quality preschools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to assure Members that the Government is committed to making preschool affordable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The expansion of Anchor and Partner Operator preschools, as well as MOE Kindergartens, ensures the supply of affordable preschool services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In addition, the Government provides subsidies to help defray the fees borne by parents, especially those from lower-income groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last year, Minister Desmond Lee shared that we are further reviewing preschool subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While this review is still ongoing, we will begin to enhance operational processes to improve access to preschool subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We agree with Mr Louis Ng and Ms Anthea Ong that we can do more to address the preschool affordability concerns of non-working mothers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Therefore, I am pleased to announce that the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) will provide more subsidies to non-working mothers who are looking for work, or who are unable to work because they are caring for a younger child.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mothers like Mdm Lee Siok Hong will benefit from this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A mother of two children, Mdm Lee cares for her younger child at home, while her elder child is enrolled in childcare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Based on our prevailing rules, Mdm Lee may qualify for $300 Basic Subsidy for her elder child until her younger child turns 18 months old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With our enhancements, Mdm Lee will receive $300 Basic Subsidy for an additional six months, until her younger child turns two years old.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Depending on her household income, Mdm Lee may also be eligible for up to $440 of means-tested Additional Subsidy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mothers who are looking for a job will also benefit from our enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under our prevailing rules, a jobseeking mother may qualify for $300 Basic Subsidy for three months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With our enhancements, she will receive $300 Basic Subsidy, and up to $440 of means-tested Additional subsidies, for six months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We hope this will give mothers greater peace of mind to secure a job.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To Mr Louis Ng's query, non-working mothers can consider enrolling their children in kindergartens, which is generally more affordable than childcare services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, today's median monthly fees are $171 for kindergartens and $856 for childcare, before subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: ECDA previously verified the working status of mothers annually.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From this year, this will be performed at fixed points in the child’s preschool years, which may be up to 2.5 years apart.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The longer timeframe between ECDA's re-assessments will give families more certainty on the amount of subsidies they receive even if the parents transit between jobs or take on caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Leon Perera asked for an update of the Early Childhood Development Centres Act which came into force from January 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This helps drive better standards across the preschool sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since 2015, ECDA has been engaging preschools to prepare for the Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: All childcare centres are already licensed under the Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Kindergartens, which are new to a licensing regime, have been provided another year to apply for a licence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand that no preschools have had to close due to the Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In fact, closures of preschools have remained consistently low over the past few years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Dr Lily Neo, Mr Darryl David and Mr Ang Hin Kee asked for an update of the Early Childhood Industry Transformation Map (ITM).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many preschools have implemented initiatives, such as technology services, centralised services and demand aggregation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These solutions help to free up our educators’ time from administrative work, so that they can focus on nurturing and teaching the children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Early Childhood ITM also aims to ensure that workers in the Early Childhood sector are well taken care of at their workplaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They will appoint a panel of experts this year to holistically examine the well-being of preschool staff, as well as recommend job redesign and workplace enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the heart of quality early childhood development are our early childhood educators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will press on to attract, develop and retain capable and passionate educators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The National Institute of Early Childhood Development will begin training its first batch of students in its full-time Diploma in Early Childhood Development and Education from April 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am also happy to announce that ECDA will soon introduce an enhanced centre management system (CMS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The CMS will interface with all preschools and improve existing processes, such as licence application and subsidy administration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With CMS, preschool administrators and parents will enjoy greater convenience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, through automation, preschools will have less data entry and no longer need to retain hardcopies of birth certificates and National Registration Identity Cards for subsidy applications.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the KidSTART pilot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: KidSTART supports parents to ensure that their children benefit from nurturing relationships, holistic child development, as well as a secure home environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are encouraged by the feedback that we have received so far.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Children are speaking more and their social skills have improved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Their parents feel better supported in their parenting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to closely assess KidSTART, and study the viability of scaling it up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Even as we continue to enhance preschool services, some of our children would need an extra helping hand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We agree with Ms Rahayu Mahzam that for young children with developmental needs, early intervention is valuable and helps them achieve their fullest potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Leon Perera asked about preschools and children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, there are 550 preschools offering the Learning and Development Support programmes catering to children with mild developmental needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We understand that insurance coverage for operators is not a barrier to enrolment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are insurers which offer group insurance coverage to preschools, without distinguishing between the developmental needs of their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Earlier this year, Minister Desmond Lee announced our plans to make early intervention services more affordable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From July, we will also progressively offer enhanced programmes that are better tailored to the different needs of children as they develop over time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Elijah was one of around 700 children who participated in our pilot of enhanced programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: He used to receive intervention at an early intervention centre twice a week, in addition to attending preschool.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After making progress, Elijah transited to receive intervention in his My First Skool preschool, where his speech therapist and preschool teachers worked together to help him gain greater independence and confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Elijah is now settling in well in a mainstream primary school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: His preschool friends also benefited from being in a more inclusive place for learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Elijah’s family appreciated the convenience of not having to shuttle between his preschool and early intervention centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During our two-year pilot, many other families and children gave positive feedback.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am optimistic that even more will benefit as we expand this offering.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will work with our partners to continually improve, so that every child in Singapore can have a good start in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In our society, we aspire to provide opportunities for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In MSF, the Office for Women’s Development (OWD) was set up as the national focal point on gender policy matters and for international cooperation pertaining to women.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There has been much progress in these areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The OWD champions the crucial roles that women play in our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam, Ms Anthea Ong and Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about how we can advance the representation of women on boards of organisations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Doing so not only helps women to advance, but benefits organisations as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This work is spearheaded by the newly formed Council for Board Diversity (CBD).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: CBD takes over from the Diversity Action Committee (DAC) and will take on a wider scope.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: DAC had suggested changes to the Code of Corporate Governance, which came into effect from January 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This Code requires companies to disclose their board diversity policies, objectives and progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We should see benefits from this in the coming years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: CBD will continue to encourage companies listed on SGX to put more women on boards but will also engage people and public sector organisations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are confident that CBD can build on this progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef also asked about the progress of BoardAgender.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Their efforts are complementary to the work of CBD.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of their key initiatives is the SG50 Champions of Change launched in 2015, which is a network of influential individuals who pledged to support the cause.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Anthea Ong highlighted the 20% pay gap between genders, derived from a ValuePenguin report.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From our understanding, the figures in this report is wider than is the case in Singapore because of the different base and definitions used.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This 10% gap can be attributed to the fact that women are more likely to exit the workforce earlier or have intermittent patterns of work, for reasons, such as child-giving.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government’s goal is, hence, to empower women with choices to enter, remain in or re-enter the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We want to support women’s desire to fulfil both their career and family aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, MOM just announced an increase in the Work-Life Grant budget and introduced various other initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will help jobseekers, including women, planning to return to the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is also critical for families to address gender equity at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Men, like me, can take on more family responsibilities, so that women do not necessarily have to shoulder the lion’s share.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam and Ms Anthea Ong also asked about other initiatives to empower women.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government is committed to working with partners to cultivate a supportive environment for women in the workplace, community and at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We also want to ensure women feel safe and protected and to come forward when they are not.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In February this year, the Criminal Law Reform Bill was tabled in Parliament for First Reading.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will allow for all women to be better protected from sexual abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To further support women, OWD actively engages the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations (SCWO).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will help women's organisations to pilot or scale up women’s development programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: More details will be shared by SCWO later this month.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SCWO also recently launched a new "SCWO Insight Series", which brings participants together with women leaders to discuss national issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SCWO will also roll out other initiatives, such as celebrating International Women's Day this Friday.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: On that note, I wish all fellow Singaporeans a meaningful International Women’s Day in advance!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, my colleagues and I at MSF will continue to work hard to uplift Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will strive to provide a good start in life for our children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will nurture a more inclusive society where Singaporeans of all abilities can live well and have peace of mind as we grow older.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will strengthen family ties because we see the family as an important institution of our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will support fellow Singaporeans who are facing challenges to get back on their feet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We do all these because we take pride in building Singapore into a nation of opportunities where all can succeed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, we will press on with this important work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We urge all Singaporeans to walk together with us in this journey to build a better tomorrow for all and our future generation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Chairman, I just have two points of clarification.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The first point would be to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: It is very heartening to hear the Minister talk about the tripartite, or should I say, the quadripartite because it involves four parties, task force.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Can the Minister share more regarding when we can expect more details on this task force in terms of a budget and opportunities and would there also be opportunities for mid-career professionals in terms of this task force's framework that is due to be set up to allow them perhaps to do a professional conversion programme, as it were?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Another point of clarification is for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The CMS would certainly help many parents to register for early childhood and so on.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Would it be compulsory for all early childhood centres to come onto this CMS programme?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And when can we expect the CMS to be rolled out into the sector?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This ensures that building on top of the skills framework that we put in place very recently for our social work professionals, we have an ecosystem where the tripartite partners understand the needs on the ground, including the new structures that we are setting up, the new kind of social safety nets that we are building, and the kinds of skillsets that our social workers will need to learn, both pre-employment and as part of continuing education, and pick up in order to be able to meet social needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There have been some preliminary sessions, but allow them to meet and discuss, and they will then come up with recommendations on the various issues I have talked about – pathway, career, transition, curriculum and so on.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I had asked another question of the Minister: would there also be opportunities for mid-career professionals, in terms of this task force's framework, to do a professional conversion programme to make the switch?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If the Minister could reply, before the Senior Parliamentary answers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Yes, indeed, this is one area that I am looking into with great interest.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I recalled Mr Dennis Tan had asked me about childcare teachers and we know that the majority of preschool teacher enrolment each year is from mid-career transitions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we are now looking with interest at the landscape for the social sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are many of them who do transit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are graduate diplomas for some of these conversions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to see how this pipeline can be further strengthened, and part of the work of the tripartite task force is also to look at this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Chairman, I agree with the Member that CMS would bring great benefits to the parents as well as the operators.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, I have one clarification for the Minister.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is actually pertaining to single unwed mothers, and I know the principles and values we want to uphold in the society and all that.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But many of the issues that they face and grapple with, I agree, can be solved at the constituency level through other networks that we have formed in the constituency and all that.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But when it comes to policy like housing, Baby Bonuses and so on, we require intervention at the Minister or Ministry level.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Pertaining to that, taking that a little bit further, I have a couple of cases where we actually have Muslim women who are second wives to Muslim men, and they are also faced with this issue where they do not qualify for Baby Bonuses and other policy issues because they are the second wives of the men.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are certain schemes which support and encourage marriage and parenthood, and these are schemes that we provide specifically for that purpose.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But having said that, we all recognise, all Members of this House recognise, that many of the single unwed mothers are not in the situation out of choice, but out of circumstance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They care for the child and they want the best for the child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And certainly, we, too, want to ensure that these children have every opportunity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, a lot of the work that we do involves ensuring that we understand fully the challenges of some of these women.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Stoic though they may be, they may need more support, and let us weave that support around them, each and every community, building that kind of support platform that I talked about earlier so that we can address them using a variety of schemes and programmes, both national, community-based and local.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the issue of Muslim wives who are second wives, there is family support that is provided to the entire family for the marriage and for parenthood, and for the children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if these families, as a whole, face challenges, whether financial or social, again, let us have a good look at the situations of these families and see how we can address some of them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier in my speech, as a result of this tighter integration of support, when the agencies can fly through the challenges of these families, flying through different policies even on the ground, and how they interface and touch families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They will be able to identify where there are gaps, where there are kinks, where there are inconsistencies which on the ground we cannot see, and if the parent Ministries can then come together and see how best we can resolve them through policies, tweaks, schemes, adjustments or even new policies, we will certainly be prepared to look at them.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Government aware of other reports that rank how well we are doing with respect to other countries?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And is this something that the Government will monitor going forward?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Unless I missed it, I do not think that was touched on.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The guillotine time is 1.00 pm, so I suggest every Member try to rush through your questions and responses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: About the study that the Member mentioned, from our understanding, that has been the only one study that had been undertaken.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If we look from the time the study was undertaken to today, we cannot deny the fact that there has been a great leap in terms of the changes that we have undertaken in terms of affordability, quality, as well as the accessibility that we have provided to our children and the families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, as a Singaporean, I feel very happy that we want to give every child a good start in life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But when we speak to parents, families and all the stakeholders, they feel that we are doing the right thing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There were, amongst others, three major criteria: one was accessibility, another was affordability and also quality, precisely the three indicators on which we are pushing very hard in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those with the lower SES, with KidSTART and with preschool outreach – going door to door for each family – we endeavour to try to raise the low SES participation rate in preschool.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we did not rank well because there was no legal mandate for it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But let us look at the results, look at the attendance rates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On quality, again, I am told we scored not so well in that study in terms of teacher-child ratio, that means, how many children there are for each teacher.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Wages, which, again, has been going up quite steadily since 2012, outpacing the general market in terms of wage increments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Preschool teacher training, again, there is the National Institute of Early Childhood Development (NIEC) and the coming together of three institutes, so, great emphasis on quality, both pre-employment as well as the professional development that we have put in place for teachers, principals, as well as educarers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And looking at the linkage between preschools and primary schools, which again now, we have strong interface because both MOE and MSF, looking after ECDA, look at the interface as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we look at our indicators where we stand and want to make sure that we invest heavily for our children to have the best start in life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If Members look at the attendance at SSOs, most of our clients turn up on weekdays.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And for those who have difficulty meeting our officers during office hours, they make arrangements with our officers at our FSCs to meet outside office hours.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we accommodate them, including those who can go to our SSOs that are open on weekends.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: The Minister mentioned earlier that he wanted to give more help to these families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I do not have the figures, but if Members look at the bottom 20% of the SES, that would be a group we would first be very concerned in ensuring that we support better, particularly if they face complex challenges.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, what I described yesterday and today is in seeing how we can weave a closer social safety net and having better social health integration in the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of resources, I am very appreciative of Members who have in this House openly sought more resources for MOM and MSF from the Finance Ministry in order for us to better strengthen this network.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We work very closely with our partners, our VWOs, those in the FSCs, child protection agencies, adult protection, family violence, as well as divorce support, and community groups, including the grassroots.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This last-mile connection on the ground is not something that any single agency can do on its own.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just a quick clarification for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just clarify that the non-working mothers will now be able to get the full basic subsidy of $300 as well as the additional subsidies?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I mentioned earlier, there are two circumstances which I highlighted: the non-working mothers who are looking for work and non-working mothers who are looking after younger children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, I would like to assure Mr Louis Ng that we would do our best to help every mother here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to see how we can facilitate caregiving and, at the same time, support them financially.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, if there are issues or things that matter that the non-working mothers are not clear about or would want to get support for, I would like to urge the families to approach any of the operators or ECDA where they can apply for special approval, and we will look at these circumstances on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, our intention is to help them, support them so that we can give the best start for our children.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: First, I would like to ask the Minister to what extent does the SSO access an applicant's wealth and assets when determining how much assistance to provide.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I am asking this in the context of data.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: With the increasing availability of data, with the advancement of technology, how might the SSO make use of this to do so, to ensure social equity?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Second is that the CKS and PDD sound quite similar.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Therefore, how do we position this to our residents and can the publicity towards these two schemes be increased just like the LPA?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: A lot of them asked about LPA, but they do not know much about these.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But, again, I reiterate that the key is we will look into this in terms of better service outreach while certainly making arrangements to accommodate the needs of our clients if they are unable to meet us during office hours.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In response to Ms Tin Pei Ling's query, the Member is right that with technology and data and with the proper linkages, we will be able to do a couple of things.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, it should be more convenient and less of a hassle for clients to have to keep churning out documents, especially if we can get them from other agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third is that this is work in progress.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a piece of work that we need to undertake with a number of the agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for CKS and PDD, I will let my colleague respond.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for the clarification.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: For the second question of publicity with greater awareness on CKS, we just piloted this service not long ago.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Once the project is piloted, when we decide it is a good scheme to roll out in the community, then we will also roll out publicity.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, would you like to withdraw your amendment please?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I have been speaking at the MSF COS for the last 13 years.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I cannot help but detect the number of cuts and the time allocated have been declining.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: This is one trend we would like to see.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But as the Minister had said, even though issues are fewer, they are becoming more complicated, more complex and it requires all of us in this sector to work more closely together.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I just want to, on behalf of all Members who spoke, extend our appreciation to everyone in the Social Service sector for their hard work, for their commitment, for their dedication.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It takes all of us to make Singapore a more caring, more inclusive and a more giving society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It is my pleasure to beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
